launch-tx-houston-memorial-park.summary: Houston's 1,500-acre urban wilderness and recreation park combines more than 30 miles of trails, the three-mile Seymour Lieberman loop, Eastern Glades, Kinder Land Bridge and Prairie, playgrounds, picnic areas, golf, tennis, swimming, sports, and visitor services.
launch-tx-houston-memorial-park.hours: Open daily 5:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m.; natural areas, staffed buildings, lots, pool, golf, tennis, and sports facilities use separate schedules.
launch-tx-houston-memorial-park.parking: About half of park parking is free. Designated paid lots use City meters at $2 per three-hour increment from 5:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m.; choose a lot near the exact destination.
launch-tx-houston-memorial-park.arrival: Use 7575 North Picnic Lane for the Cullen Running Trails Center, or navigate directly to Eastern Glades, Kinder Land Bridge, Picnic Loop, golf, tennis, pool, Arboretum, or the intended trailhead.
launch-tx-houston-memorial-park.restrooms: Restrooms are available at the Cullen Running Trails Center, Eastern Glades, along the Seymour Lieberman loop, and near selected recreation facilities; hours vary by location.
launch-tx-houston-memorial-park.cost: General park, trails, prairie, playground, and landscape access are free. Metered parking, golf, tennis, pool, reservations, showers, food, and programs may cost separately.
launch-tx-houston-memorial-park.accessibility: The Seymour Lieberman Trail and Eastern Glades are wheelchair accessible; rugged Bayou Wilds and natural trails vary in surface, grade, roots, mud, and drainage.
launch-tx-houston-memorial-park.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed and are prohibited on the Roy H. Cullen Timing Track; natural trails and prairie are not off-leash areas.
launch-tx-houston-memorial-park.family: Vale-Asche Playground, Eastern Glades, picnic areas, the loop, and seasonal pool serve families, but destinations are widely separated across 1,500 acres.
launch-tx-houston-memorial-park.transit: METRO Route 20 serves Memorial Drive stops inside the park and Route 84 stops near West Loop North and Woodway; plan for the exact destination.
launch-tx-houston-memorial-park.need: The western Outer Loop Trail remains closed for Memorial Groves construction into 2027. Check live trail and event status, bring water, and do not enter bayous or Hines Lake.

launch-tx-houston-hermann-park.summary: Houston's major Museum District park links The Commons and Play Gardens, free gardens, splash pad, pedal-boat lake, railroad, carousel, golf, Miller Outdoor Theatre, reflection pool, zoo, museums, lawns, and picnic areas.
launch-tx-houston-hermann-park.hours: Open daily 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m.; gardens, railroad, carousel, pedal boats, zoo, museums, cafes, theatre, and golf use separate schedules.
launch-tx-houston-hermann-park.parking: Use free Lots F, G, and H for the zoo, lake, railroad, and Commons; Lot C for Centennial Gardens; or Lots D and E for Miller Outdoor Theatre. Busy weekends fill quickly.
launch-tx-houston-hermann-park.arrival: Route to the exact destination. The Commons, gardens, theatre, zoo, museums, and lake form separate clusters across the 445-acre park.
launch-tx-houston-hermann-park.restrooms: Dependable locations include Lake Plaza, Centennial Gardens, Miller Outdoor Theatre, Japanese Garden, The Commons, Bayou Parkland Pavilion, golf clubhouse, and Judson Robinson Jr. Community Center.
launch-tx-houston-hermann-park.cost: The park, gardens, playgrounds, splash pad, paths, lawns, and Miller Outdoor Theatre hillside are free. Zoo, museum, train, carousel, boats, golf, food, and some events charge separately.
launch-tx-houston-hermann-park.accessibility: Paved routes connect major destinations, but distances are substantial; choose the nearest lot or METRORail stop and verify destination-specific routes.
launch-tx-houston-hermann-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed in general areas and McWilliams Dog Park is the designated off-leash area. Pets are excluded from rides, boats, play gardens, water play, and buildings except service animals.
launch-tx-houston-hermann-park.family: One of Houston's strongest family destinations, with major play gardens, free splash pad, train, carousel, boats, zoo, museums, gardens, lawns, and shade areas.
launch-tx-houston-hermann-park.transit: METRORail Museum District and Memorial Hermann Hospital/Houston Zoo stations provide practical access; choose based on the destination.
launch-tx-houston-hermann-park.need: Attractions can close independently for weather, maintenance, events, or seasonal operations. Houston heat and lightning make early arrival, water, shade planning, and a confirmed refuge important.

launch-tx-houston-buffalo-bayou-park.summary: A 160-acre downtown bayou corridor with skyline trails, a nature playground and water feature, dog park, skatepark, gardens, lawns, paddling access, public art, visitor facilities, and the underground 1926 Cistern.
launch-tx-houston-buffalo-bayou-park.hours: Open daily 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m.; Cistern tours, visitor facilities, rentals, food, and programs use separate schedules.
launch-tx-houston-buffalo-bayou-park.parking: Metered spaces between Sabine and Taft are $1 for up to three hours. Additional signed parking is near City Lot H and Allen Parkway; never park on grass or flood-control access.
launch-tx-houston-buffalo-bayou-park.arrival: Use The Water Works at 105-B Sabine Street for the Cistern and nature play area, 2929 Allen Parkway for Johnny Steele Dog Park, or navigate directly to the intended trail access.
launch-tx-houston-buffalo-bayou-park.restrooms: The Water Works restrooms are generally open 8:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m.; Lost Lake restrooms generally operate 8:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. Long trail sections have no nearby restroom.
launch-tx-houston-buffalo-bayou-park.cost: General park, trails, playground, dog park, skatepark, lawns, gardens, and public art are free. Parking, Cistern tours, rentals, food, permits, and events may charge.
launch-tx-houston-buffalo-bayou-park.accessibility: Paved trails and plazas serve major destinations, while sand, grass, slopes, wet steps, and flood-prone low routes vary substantially.
launch-tx-houston-buffalo-bayou-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed generally; Johnny Steele Dog Park is the designated off-leash area and may close independently after flooding or water-quality concerns.
launch-tx-houston-buffalo-bayou-park.family: The nature play area and designed stream are strong family draws, but Buffalo Bayou itself is active floodwater and is not a swimming or wading area.
launch-tx-houston-buffalo-bayou-park.transit: METRO Route 20 follows Memorial Drive near the park; enter the exact destination because the corridor stretches for miles.
launch-tx-houston-buffalo-bayou-park.need: Low trails, underpasses, paddling access, and the dog park can close after storms, high water, sediment, or contamination. Obey barriers and use upper routes.

launch-tx-houston-discovery-green.summary: Downtown Houston's 12-acre village green combines a major playground, free interactive fountain, Kinder Lake, separate dog runs, event lawns, performance spaces, public art, restaurants, gardens, and frequent free programming.
launch-tx-houston-discovery-green.hours: Open daily 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. Restrooms operate 9:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m.; fountain changing rooms 9:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m.; events and seasonal attractions vary.
launch-tx-houston-discovery-green.parking: Use metered perimeter streets or paid downtown garages, including Avenida Central beneath the park. Convention, arena, festival, and event traffic can sharply affect price and availability.
launch-tx-houston-discovery-green.arrival: Use the Alkek Building and Gateway Fountain on the northwest side for information, restrooms, playground, and family water play; select the lake, stage, or dog-run edge for those destinations.
launch-tx-houston-discovery-green.restrooms: Public restrooms are on the south side of the Alkek Building near the playground and generally operate 9:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m.; a women's restroom is also in Avenida Central Garage.
launch-tx-houston-discovery-green.cost: Admission, playground, fountain, lawns, dog runs, public art, and most public programming are free. Parking, food, boats, skating, rentals, and selected events cost separately.
launch-tx-houston-discovery-green.accessibility: Broad paved paths and level plazas serve the compact park; wheelchair users can participate in some seasonal rink experiences under posted rules.
launch-tx-houston-discovery-green.dogs: Pets must be leashed outside the separate large- and small-dog runs. Dog-run users must remain with dogs and follow size, vaccination, and 45-minute rules.
launch-tx-houston-discovery-green.family: Excellent compact family destination with a refreshed hill playground, free Gateway Fountain, lake, lawns, restrooms, changing rooms, and frequent programs.
launch-tx-houston-discovery-green.transit: METRORail, downtown buses, convention-district walking routes, and nearby bike facilities make transit practical; Convention District is the closest rail stop.
launch-tx-houston-discovery-green.need: Gateway Fountain generally runs 9:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. and shuts off for thunder or lightning. Private events and maintenance can close portions of the compact park.

launch-tx-houston-levy-park.summary: Upper Kirby's compact destination park pairs an imaginative gated Children's Park and water feature with a tree-canopy overlook, dog park, game carts, reading room, lawns, pavilion, concessions, gardens, and daily programming.
launch-tx-houston-levy-park.hours: General outdoor areas follow posted park hours; the Children's Park operates 8:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m. and closes the first Tuesday monthly from 8:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m. for maintenance.
launch-tx-houston-levy-park.parking: Free parking is available adjacent to the park and along Eastside Street and Wakeforest Avenue. Paid overflow is available in the Kirby Grove garage at Richmond and Wakeforest.
launch-tx-houston-levy-park.arrival: Use Eastside Street for the Children's Park and central pavilion, or select Wakeforest Avenue and the east side for parking, concessions, Event Lawn, and Dog Park.
launch-tx-houston-levy-park.restrooms: Family restrooms and changing facilities support the Children's Park; confirm posted access when the gated children's area is closed for maintenance or events.
launch-tx-houston-levy-park.cost: Park entry, playground, water feature, dog park, reading room, lawns, games, and most daily activities are free. Garage parking, concessions, rentals, and selected events cost separately.
launch-tx-houston-levy-park.accessibility: Paved paths, gradual ramps, the Treehouse Overlook boardwalk, family restrooms, and compact layout support accessible visits; some play elements require transfer or climbing.
launch-tx-houston-levy-park.dogs: Dogs are allowed in the designated large- and small-dog areas under posted rules; pets are not allowed inside the Children's Park or its water feature.
launch-tx-houston-levy-park.family: A high-value family stop with imaginative play, broad slide, climbing, tunnels, chimes, a three-tier water feature, shade seating, restrooms, lawn games, and food nearby.
launch-tx-houston-levy-park.transit: Local METRO buses serve Richmond Avenue and the Upper Kirby area; walking from the nearest stop is more practical than rail.
launch-tx-houston-levy-park.need: Children under 12 require an accompanying adult, flat shoes are required, surfaces can become hot, and the water feature requires swim diapers for children under two.

launch-tx-houston-emancipation-park.summary: Houston's historic Juneteenth park and Third Ward community center includes an aquatics center, three sprayground areas, playground, cultural and recreation buildings, Blessing Theater, gym, baseball, tennis, pavilions, programs, and major commemorative events.
launch-tx-houston-emancipation-park.hours: Outdoor areas and staffed facilities use posted schedules; pool, spraygrounds, recreation center, gym, cultural center, and programs may open or close independently.
launch-tx-houston-emancipation-park.parking: Free parallel parking is available on Emancipation Avenue and Hutchins Street, head-in spaces line Tuam Street, and a 55-space lot with ADA and EV spaces sits across from the baseball field.
launch-tx-houston-emancipation-park.arrival: Use Emancipation Avenue for the pool and central frontage or Tuam Street for the baseball field, main lot, recreation facilities, and easier event orientation.
launch-tx-houston-emancipation-park.restrooms: Restrooms are associated with the aquatics, recreation, cultural, and event facilities and follow staffed hours; verify before depending on a building during early or late outdoor use.
launch-tx-houston-emancipation-park.cost: Outdoor park access, playground, spraygrounds, courts, and many community programs are free. Pool registration, rentals, classes, and special events may use separate rules or fees.
launch-tx-houston-emancipation-park.accessibility: ADA parking is available in front of the pool and in the Tuam Street lot; paved routes connect the renovated central facilities and outdoor areas.
launch-tx-houston-emancipation-park.dogs: Leashed pets may use general outdoor areas under park rules but are excluded from pool, sprayground, playground, courts, fields, and indoor facilities except service animals.
launch-tx-houston-emancipation-park.family: The playground, outdoor spraygrounds, pool, gym, pavilions, fields, and cultural programming make this a major family and community destination.
launch-tx-houston-emancipation-park.transit: METRORail's Ensemble/HCC station and local bus routes provide access, with a walk into Third Ward; verify the best route for events.
launch-tx-houston-emancipation-park.need: Construction associated with the cultural expansion may temporarily affect the Cultural Center and adjacent lawn while most playground, sprayground, and sports areas remain available; check current notices.

launch-tx-houston-gerald-d-hines-waterwa.summary: Houston's iconic 64-foot semicircular Waterwall creates a dramatic mist-filled public landmark opposite Williams Tower, framed by live oaks and lawns in the Uptown district near the Galleria.
launch-tx-houston-gerald-d-hines-waterwa.hours: Open daily 9:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m.; fountain operation can pause for maintenance, severe weather, freezing conditions, or special work.
launch-tx-houston-gerald-d-hines-waterwa.parking: The most convenient official recommendation is paid visitor parking at Williams Tower, followed by a short walk. Do not assume adjacent curbs or private business lots permit park parking.
launch-tx-houston-gerald-d-hines-waterwa.arrival: Approach from Post Oak Boulevard or the Williams Tower visitor garage and follow the pedestrian path south to the fountain; the Waterwall itself is the central destination.
launch-tx-houston-gerald-d-hines-waterwa.restrooms: There is no dependable dedicated public restroom inside the small outdoor park; use a confirmed open nearby business or facility rather than assuming Williams Tower access.
launch-tx-houston-gerald-d-hines-waterwa.cost: The park and Waterwall are free. Garage parking and nearby food or shopping cost separately.
launch-tx-houston-gerald-d-hines-waterwa.accessibility: Level paved approaches reach the fountain plaza and lawns, but spray can make surfaces wet and slick; use care with mobility devices near the basin.
launch-tx-houston-gerald-d-hines-waterwa.dogs: Leashed dogs may use the outdoor lawn and paths under posted rules; keep pets out of the fountain basin and away from crowded photo areas.
launch-tx-houston-gerald-d-hines-waterwa.family: The roar, mist, scale, and live-oak lawn make a memorable short family stop, but the fountain basin is not a splash pad or swimming area.
launch-tx-houston-gerald-d-hines-waterwa.transit: METRO buses serve Post Oak Boulevard and the Uptown corridor; the park is walkable from the Galleria area but not adjacent to rail.
launch-tx-houston-gerald-d-hines-waterwa.need: Expect heavy mist and wet pavement close to the Waterwall. Supervise children, protect cameras and phones, and never enter or climb the fountain structure.

launch-tx-houston-smither-park.summary: A free half-acre community-built mosaic environment beside the Orange Show, with a 400-foot Memory Wall, amphitheater, pavilion, swings, meditation wall, shell-covered paths, marble tower, and more than 300 contributing artists.
launch-tx-houston-smither-park.hours: Open daily from dawn until dusk. Saturday artist activity and scheduled programs are weather dependent; the adjacent Orange Show Monument has separate hours and may be closed for restoration.
launch-tx-houston-smither-park.parking: Event and campus parking is directed to 2334 Gulf Terminal Drive. On ordinary visits, follow posted Orange Show campus parking and avoid blocking neighborhood access.
launch-tx-houston-smither-park.arrival: Enter from Munger Street for the mosaic park; use the exact Smither Park pin because the Orange Show Monument and administrative campus are adjacent but separate destinations.
launch-tx-houston-smither-park.restrooms: Do not assume a public restroom is available during every dawn-to-dusk park visit; nearby Orange Show facilities follow their own operating and event schedules.
launch-tx-houston-smither-park.cost: Smither Park admission is always free. Donations, special classes, merchandise, and some Orange Show programs may cost separately.
launch-tx-houston-smither-park.accessibility: The compact park uses mosaic-covered plaza and walkway surfaces; most landmarks are close together, but decorative textures, heat, and event crowds can affect movement.
launch-tx-houston-smither-park.dogs: Leashed dogs may visit outdoor areas under posted rules; keep them off mosaic art, planted areas, swings, and programmed gathering spaces.
launch-tx-houston-smither-park.family: The colors, found-object details, swings, tower, walls, and chance to watch artists work make this unusually engaging for children, with close supervision around fragile art.
launch-tx-houston-smither-park.transit: Local METRO bus routes serve the East End and Third Ward edges; most visitors drive, rideshare, cycle, or combine the stop with nearby Orange Show destinations.
launch-tx-houston-smither-park.need: This is an evolving work of public art, not a conventional playground. Do not climb mosaics, remove objects, or treat the artwork as play equipment; Saturdays are the best chance to see artists working, weather permitting.
